name: Immanence of Set — 2 Intermediate — Voice of the Prophet

system.description:
In ancient times, the words of the oracle could change a mortal life forever, elevating great heroes or dooming them, depending on how they interpreted the pronouncements of the god. The Setites were often the serpent lingering in the shadows of oracular temples such as Siwa or Delphi, sharing the corrupting words of the god with supplicants seeking confirmation of their own fears or ambitions. When a Setite invokes this power, he is supposedly communicating with his akh, lingering in the otherworld and drawing on the supernatural knowledge available there.

System: The Setite invokes this power to deliver a prophetic vision or utterance to a listener seeking guidance. As with any divination, the truth of the vision is only as clear as the Storyteller wishes; a listener who acts upon the prophecy may find their own choices twisting the vision toward its fulfillment, whether or not the prophecy was ever objectively true, much as a merchant who is promised seven ships of gold will beggar himself chasing the vision even as fortune turns against him.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Three: Serpents
